conv_286.speaker: Cobbled_Envoy
conv_286.text: Friends, I have a proposal for any house with a standing army and some patience. Shall we discuss it over wine, Slugg?

conv_286.speaker: Slugg
conv_286.text: Wine, yes. Your schemes, no. Last time they cost me forty bolts of wool.

conv_286.speaker: SerCrowmere
conv_286.text: Saaravenn Fen can muster {troop_count} blades for an honest cause. Let the rolls record who stood with us.

conv_286.speaker: Cobbled_Envoy
conv_286.text: Honest causes pay in gold, SerCrowmere. Lauresse offers {gold} for the first {village} we take together.

conv_286.speaker: Slugg
conv_286.text: Gold is fine, Envoy. My wool is 40 a bolt, first come, and it does not come with a lecture.

conv_286.speaker: SerCrowmere
conv_286.text: Gold does not buy an honest banner, Slugg. The rolls shall record who came with blades.

conv_287.speaker: DawnwatchSeal
conv_287.text: I still hear the horns from the Night of {village}, when the Ighrast line held firm against every banner. Do you remember it, Eeel?

conv_287.speaker: Eeel
conv_287.text: remember it. the line held because the flank was stupid. we watched the ratio collapse at {town} and called it a plan

conv_287.speaker: DawnwatchSeal
conv_287.text: The ratio was never the question. Our oath was, and we kept it with {troop_count} shields on the wall.

conv_287.speaker: Eeel
conv_287.text: gg. you kept it with {troop_count} shields and lost the wall anyway

conv_287.speaker: DawnwatchSeal
conv_287.text: Lost the wall, perhaps, but not the honour. Let the dawn witness the oath, Eeel.

conv_287.speaker: Eeel
conv_287.text: the dawn saw your back as you ran. not my problem

conv_288.speaker: DameBeaneOfQuel
conv_288.text: Let it be said plainly: pikes are the spine of any army. Let the causeways remember this, TurnipTheFlank.

conv_288.speaker: TurnipTheFlank
conv_288.text: pikes break on the first charge. ur spine is a stick

conv_288.speaker: Glovaric_Ironhand
conv_288.text: Hear this: the glove shall not yield. {troop_count} knights outlast any pike wall. Mind your tongue, TurnipTheFlank.

conv_288.speaker: DameBeaneOfQuel
conv_288.text: Knights are a gilded luxury, and gilded things break at the first real press.

conv_288.speaker: TurnipTheFlank
conv_288.text: ur line broke at minute 4 last time. gg tho

conv_288.speaker: Glovaric_Ironhand
conv_288.text: Minute 4 was a feint, and you know it. The glove remembers every field.

conv_288.speaker: TurnipTheFlank
conv_288.text: feint or not the pikes held the middle. thats the whole argument

conv_289.speaker: xX_EmberQuill_Xx
conv_289.text: I raise this matter before the council, HoneyHelm. Nobody remembers the war at {village} as well as I do.

conv_289.speaker: HoneyHelm
conv_289.text: Ser xX_EmberQuill_Xx, I remember it as a feast of honour, not a ledger of debts.

conv_289.speaker: xX_EmberQuill_Xx
conv_289.text: Honour is a fine word for a banner. Ledgers are what win the peace. We still owe {gold} to the houses who marched.

conv_289.speaker: HoneyHelm
conv_289.text: Our banners marched for the Confederacy, not for coin. May they meet in honour again, Ser xX_EmberQuill_Xx.

conv_289.speaker: xX_EmberQuill_Xx
conv_289.text: Then let us meet in honour, and we shall see who keeps the ledger honest. {troop_count} men will watch.
